context: Following up on the disaster days later
purpose: Track the aftermath; teach 当局/死亡/異常/宣言/強制/減少/戦い/処分

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: あの災害、その後の状況はどうですか？
lines.en: That disaster — how’s the situation since?
lines.style: concerned student following up, voice clear and distinctly their own

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 当局の発表では、死亡者数は確定したそうです。
lines.en: Per the authorities, the death toll is now confirmed.
lines.style: measured teacher delivering the update, tone holding steady through the whole line

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 異常気象は今後も増えるんでしょうか。
lines.style: worried teen looking ahead, delivery emotionally grounded and unforced

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 専門家がそう宣言しています。
lines.style: teacher citing the expert view, spoken with a recognizable personal cadence

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 避難の強制は解除されたんですか？
lines.en: Has the forced evacuation been lifted?
lines.style: student checking the current status, each word carrying genuine natural feeling

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: ええ、危険が減少したと判断されました。
lines.en: Yes, the danger was judged to have decreased.
lines.style: teacher giving the reassuring news, voice clear and distinctly their own

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 復興は、まさに時間との戦いですね。
lines.en: Recovery is truly a battle against time.
lines.style: reflective teen voicing empathy, tone holding steady through the whole line

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 大量のがれきの処分が課題だと聞きます。
lines.en: I hear disposing of the rubble is a challenge.
lines.style: informed student noting the obstacle, delivery emotionally grounded and unforced
